mainTopic: Deathbed gifts and money sent through a שליח, then the opening משנה of the second פרק on an agent who saw only part of a גט being written or signed
overview: The עמוד opens with the end of the רבנן's proof story. A dying mother gave her valuable brooch to her daughter, and the חכמים honored it. רבי אלעזר rejects the proof, saying the sons of רוכל were wicked. The גמרא then lines up every opinion in the ברייתא about money sent through a שליח. Each one depends on two questions: is a real קנין needed, and is it a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead? A side question about whether רבי שמעון הנשיא was himself a נשיא ends in תיקו. The גמרא then defends רב יוסף's ruling by setting it in the case of a healthy sender who is still alive. After the הדרן, the second פרק opens with a משנה about an agent who saw only part of a גט being written or signed, or whose testimony is split with someone else. The גמרא explains why this משנה is needed, clarifies which half was written in front of him, and brings רב חסדא's ruling that the two ways of proving a גט cannot be mixed. רבא challenges that reasoning and begins his own explanation, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The brooch story: the Sages honored a dying woman's gift
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן finish their story against רבי אלעזר. A sick woman said to give her very valuable brooch to her daughter, she died, and the חכמים carried out her words.
steps.simpleTranslation: "[Give] my brooch to my daughter," and it was worth twelve מנה. She died, and the Sages fulfilled her words!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן are finishing a proof story. It shows that the words of a dying person work even without a formal act of acquiring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that a שכיב מרע (a dying person) still needs a real קנין to give a gift. The רבנן point to a real case where the חכמים honored a deathbed gift that was only spoken, and a big one too. If the חכמים did that, it seems words alone are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: my brooch, a piece of jewelry
a unit of money worth one hundred דינרים
and the Sages fulfilled her words
a person who is seriously ill and may be dying

phrases.english: [Give] my brooch to my daughter,
phrases.notes: The story begins on the previous עמוד. This is the sick mother speaking.

phrases.english: and it was worth twelve מנה,
and she died, and the Sages fulfilled her words!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבִינְתִּי לְבִתִּי, וְהִיא בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבנן's story, which began before this section, aimed against רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That a שכיב מרע's spoken gift works without a קנין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case: the mother of the sons of רוכל and her brooch.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר pushes the story aside
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers with a curse on the sons of רוכל. He means they were wicked, so the case proves nothing about the normal law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "The sons of רוכל, let their mother bury them!"
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר rejects the רבנן's proof. He says that case was special because of who the sons were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons were wicked, so the חכמים deliberately let their mother's gift go to her daughter and kept it out of the sons' inheritance. That was a special decision about these people, not the regular law. So the story does not prove that words alone work.

keyTerms.meaning: may their mother bury them, a curse that they should die young

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not denying that the story happened. He agrees the חכמים honored her gift, but says it was a one-time decision because of the sons, not proof of the general rule.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר, answering the רבנן.

phrases.english: The sons of רוכל, let their mother bury them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: בְּנֵי רוֹכֵל תִּקְבְּרֵם אִמָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the story. רבי אלעזר's own position stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case was a special decision about wicked heirs, not the regular law.

steps.title: Sorting the first opinions of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the תנא קמא and רבי נתן with רבי יעקב follow רבי אלעזר. They add that there is no מצוה to fulfill the dead person's words. The יש אומרים follow רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא follows רבי אלעזר. רבי נתן and רבי יעקב also follow רבי אלעזר: even though the sender died, we do not say it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead. The "יש אומרים" follow the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא about money sent through a שליח when the sender died. It starts matching each opinion to one side of the רבי אלעזר and רבנן debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions. Do words alone transfer ownership, as the רבנן say, or is a real קנין needed, as רבי אלעזר says? And even without a קנין, is it a מצוה to carry out a dead person's wishes? רבי נתן and רבי יעקב need a קנין and also reject the מצוה idea. The יש אומרים simply hold that words alone work.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead
some say, an opinion in the ברייתא introduced this way

steps.confusionAlert: Siding with רבי אלעזר does not settle the case by itself. A תנא can need a real קנין and still require us to carry out the dead person's wishes because of the מצוה. Keep these two questions separate.

phrases.english: The first תנא follows רבי אלעזר;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי נָתָן וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב נָמֵי כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: and רבי נתן and רבי יעקב also follow רבי אלעזר –
even though he died,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person who sent the money.

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִצְוָה לְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי הַמֵּת;
phrases.english: we do not say it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead;
and the "some say" follow the רבנן;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the רבי אלעזר and רבנן debate clear, the גמרא uses it to explain the ברייתא's opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא and רבי נתן with רבי יעקב follow רבי אלעזר, with no מצוה to fulfill the dead's words. The יש אומרים follow רבנן.

steps.title: רבי יהודה הנשיא: a קנין is needed, but there is a מצוה to fulfill the dead's words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא, quoting רבי מאיר, follows רבי אלעזר that words alone do not transfer ownership. But once the sender has died, there is a מצוה to carry out his wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא, who spoke in the name of רבי מאיר, follows רבי אלעזר. But where the sender died, we say it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues mapping the ברייתא with the next opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הנשיא agrees with רבי אלעזר on the basic rule that a real קנין is needed. He parts ways with רבי נתן and רבי יעקב on the second question: once the sender has died, his wishes are carried out because of the מצוה. So the outcome can differ even though the basic legal view is the same.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the מצוה to fulfill the dead's words is a separate reason to give the money, apart from the laws of קנין.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר –
phrases.english: And רבי יהודה הנשיא, who spoke in the name of רבי מאיר –
follows רבי אלעזר,
however, where he died,
we say it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the mapping and sets up a contrast with רבי נתן and רבי יעקב on the מצוה question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real קנין is needed, but once the sender has died there is a מצוה to fulfill his words.

steps.title: The last opinions: divide it, the agent's judgment, and a story
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים who say "divide it" are unsure of the law. The ones who say "here they said" hold that the agent's own judgment decides. רבי שמעון הנשיא only adds a real-life case, not a new opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: they should divide it, because they are unsure. The opinion that says "here they said" holds that the agent's judgment is better. רבי שמעון הנשיא came only to tell us a story that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes mapping the ברייתא by explaining the last three voices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dividing the money is a way of handling doubt, since the חכמים cannot decide between the two sides. "שודא עדיף" leaves the decision to the agent's judgment. רבי שמעון הנשיא is not a new side in the debate; he reports a case that happened.

keyTerms.meaning: the agent's own judgment is better

steps.whatToRemember: Every opinion in the ברייתא answers two questions. First, is a real קנין needed, as רבי אלעזר says, or are words enough, as רבנן say? Second, is it a מצוה to fulfill the dead's words? The "divide it" and "agent's judgment" views are ways of handling doubt.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: they should divide it –
because they are unsure;
and "here they said": the agent's judgment is better;
phrases.notes: "Here they said" are the opening words of another opinion in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and רבי שמעון הנשיא –
came to teach us a story that happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the mapping of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "Divide it" comes from doubt. "Here they said" relies on the agent's judgment. רבי שמעון הנשיא only reports a case.

steps.title: Was רבי שמעון הנשיא himself a נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: The learners ask what the title in רבי שמעון הנשיא means. Was he himself a נשיא, or was he quoting a נשיא?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: רבי שמעון הנשיא — was he a נשיא, or was he speaking in the name of a נשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the name רבי שמעון הנשיא. This sets up an attempt to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "רבי שמעון הנשיא" can be read two ways. Either הנשיא is his own title, or it means he said this in the name of the נשיא. This is a question about how to read a name, not about the law of the case.

keyTerms.meaning: they asked, an open question raised in the בית מדרש
the head of the Jewish community

phrases.english: They asked:
רבי שמעון הנשיא:
is he a נשיא,
or is he speaking in the name of a נשיא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the name רבי שמעון הנשיא from step 5 and asks what the title means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הנשיא is his own title or means he was quoting the נשיא.

steps.title: A try: רב יוסף calls him רבי שמעון הנשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from רב יוסף, who said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון הנשיא, that this name belongs to a real person who was a נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יוסף said, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון הנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof to answer the question. רב יוסף speaks of רבי שמעון הנשיא as one person whose view is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב יוסף rules like "רבי שמעון הנשיא" as one person, it sounds like that is his real name and title. That would suggest he himself was a נשיא.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for רב יוסף said:
The הלכה follows רבי שמעון הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון הנשיא was himself a נשיא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ruling: הלכה כרבי שמעון הנשיא.

steps.title: The proof does not settle it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question is still open. רב יוסף may just be using the name as the ברייתא gives it, without telling us what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you can still ask: is he a נשיא, or is he speaking in the name of a נשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רב יוסף. The same doubt applies to his words too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף used the same words, "רבי שמעון הנשיא," that the ברייתא used. His wording has the same two possible meanings, so it adds nothing new.

phrases.english: But you can still ask:
is he a נשיא,
or is he speaking in the name of a נשיא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from רב יוסף.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף's words have the same two possible meanings as the ברייתא's, so they cannot decide the question.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The question is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether רבי שמעון הנשיא was himself a נשיא or was quoting one. So the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand, meaning the question is left open

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether רבי שמעון הנשיא was himself a נשיא ends in תיקו. רב יוסף's ruling does not settle it.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 6 after the proof failed in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unresolved: we do not know if רבי שמעון הנשיא was himself a נשיא or was speaking in a נשיא's name.

steps.title: Going back to רב יוסף's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב יוסף's statement that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון הנשיא, so it can look at it more closely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main point: רב יוסף said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון הנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב יוסף's ruling that was mentioned earlier. This sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רב יוסף's words were only used to ask what the title 'הנשיא' means. Now the גמרא looks at the ruling itself: the money goes back to the sender's side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself.' The גמרא goes back to a statement it mentioned earlier, to study it on its own
The practical law follows this opinion

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to רב יוסף's statement from step 7, this time to look at the ruling itself.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon HaNasi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier, the גמרא used this line only to discuss the name. Now it returns to the ruling itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון הנשיא: the money goes back to the sender's side, not to the recipient's heirs.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule about a dying person's words
steps.stepSummary: The words of a שכיב מרע count as if written and handed over. So the gift should already belong to the recipient, and his heirs should get the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we hold that what a dying person says counts as if it were written down and handed over?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's ruling with a well-known rule about a dying person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sender was a שכיב מרע, his words alone make the gift take effect, even before the money arrives. Then the money already belongs to the recipient, and it should go to his heirs, not back to the sender's side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But don't we hold...' A way of bringing an accepted rule as a challenge
They count as if written down and handed over

phrases.english: But don't we hold
that the words of a person on his deathbed
are like written and delivered!
phrases.notes: The idea: his spoken gift works as if a document were written and given over, so the gift takes effect at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן דִּבְרֵי שְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that the money goes back to the sender's side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dying person's words make the gift take effect right away, so the money already belongs to the recipient and should go to his heirs.

steps.title: רב יוסף is talking about a healthy sender
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's ruling is about a sender who was healthy, not a שכיב מרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף explains the case as one where the sender was healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sender in this case was a healthy person, so the special rule for a dying person does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy person's gift only takes effect when the money reaches the recipient. Since the recipient died first, the gift never took effect, and the money stays with the sender's side.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it in a specific case

phrases.english: Rav Yosef sets it
in the case of a healthy person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sender was dying, so his words alone gave the money to the recipient.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sender was healthy, so the gift never took effect.

steps.title: Challenge: the sender has died, and we must carry out the words of the dead
steps.stepSummary: The ruling says 'return it to the sender's heirs,' so the sender has died. There is a מצוה to carry out a dead person's wishes, so the money should be given as he asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said the money goes to the sender's heirs, and we hold that it is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 12. Even if the sender was healthy when he sent the money, he has since died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the sender's heirs' show that the sender is no longer alive. Since we must fulfill a dead person's wishes, his instruction to give the money should be carried out, and not cancelled by sending it back to his heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to carry out what a dead person asked

phrases.english: But he says it goes to the heirs of the sender,
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבי שמעון הנשיא, whose ruling רב יוסף follows. Mentioning heirs tells us the sender has died.

phrases.english: and we hold:
it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 using the wording of the ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the sender was healthy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording shows the sender has died, and there is a מצוה to carry out a dead person's wishes, so the money should not go back to his heirs.

steps.title: Change the wording: return it to the sender
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording to 'return it to the sender,' so the sender is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it this way: 'They should return it to the sender.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the challenge by changing the wording: the money goes back to the sender himself, not to his heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sender is alive, there is no 'words of the dead' to carry out. He was healthy, the recipient died before getting the money, so the gift never took effect and the money simply goes back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: They should return it to the sender

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's ruling ends up being about a healthy sender who is still alive. The recipient died before the money reached him, so it goes back to the sender.

phrases.english: Teach it this way:
They should return it to the sender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The text says 'to the sender's heirs,' which means the sender has died.
steps.terutzMaskana: The text should say 'to the sender.' He is alive, so there is no dead person's wish to carry out.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter הַמֵּבִיא קַמָּא
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of גיטין comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, first פרק of הַמֵּבִיא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line for the first פרק of מסכת גיטין. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first and second פרקים both start with the words הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט. So the first one is called הַמֵּבִיא קַמָּא, 'the first הַמֵּבִיא.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you.' A closing formula said at the end of a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, the first 'One who brings'
phrases.notes: Both the first and second פרקים open with הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט, so this one is called 'the first.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the discussion ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of גיטין is finished.

steps.title: New chapter: an agent who saw only part of the writing or signing
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if the agent bringing a גט from overseas saw only the writing, only the signing, or only part of one of them, the גט is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone brings a גט from overseas and says 'It was written in front of me but not signed in front of me,' or 'signed in front of me but not written in front of me,' or 'all of it was written in front of me and half of it signed in front of me,' or 'half of it was written in front of me and all of it signed in front of me,' it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The second פרק opens with a משנה about an agent who did not see the whole גט being written and signed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent needs to have seen both the writing and the signing in full. The משנה lists four ways of seeing only part, and in all four the גט is invalid. 'Half signed' means he saw only one of the two witnesses sign.

keyTerms.meaning: A country overseas, outside ארץ ישראל
It was written in front of me
It was signed in front of me

steps.confusionAlert: Even if the agent saw all of the writing, or all of the signing, it is not enough. He must have seen both in full.

phrases.english: One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,
and said: 'It was written in front of me
but it was not signed in front of me';
'It was signed in front of me
but it was not written in front of me';
'All of it was written in front of me
and half of it was signed in front of me';
phrases.notes: 'Half signed' means he saw only one of the two witnesses sign.

phrases.english: 'Half of it was written in front of me
and all of it was signed in front of me' –
it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An agent who saw only part of the writing or only part of the signing cannot make the גט valid. It is פסול.

steps.title: The rest of the משנה: when the writing and the signing are seen by different people
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If one person saw the writing and another saw the signing, the גט is פסול. If two saw the writing and one saw the signing, it is also פסול, but רבי יהודה says כשר. If one saw the writing and two saw the signing, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one person says 'It was written in front of me' and another says 'It was signed in front of me,' the גט is invalid. If two say 'It was written in front of us' and one says 'It was signed in front of me,' it is invalid, but רבי יהודה says it is valid. If one says 'It was written in front of me' and two say 'It was signed in front of us,' it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of cases where the agent's testimony is split up between different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special trust חז"ל gave the agent works only when one person testifies to both the writing and the signing. When the testimony is split between two people, that special trust does not apply, so the גט is פסול. The last case is כשר because two people confirm the signing, which is the normal way any document is verified, and one person is enough to testify about the writing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was written in my presence', the agent's statement about the writing
'It was signed in my presence', the agent's statement about the signing

phrases.english: One says: "It was written in my presence"
and another one says: "It was signed in my presence": it is invalid.
Two say: "It was written in our presence"
and one says: "It was signed in my presence": it is invalid;
and רבי יהודה rules it valid.
One says: "It was written in my presence"
and two say: "It was signed in our presence": it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּפָנַי נִכְתַּב וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּפָנַי נֶחְתַּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה begun in step 16 with more cases of split testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the writing and the signing are seen by different people, the גט is פסול, unless the signing is confirmed by two people. In the case of two for the writing and one for the signing, רבי יהודה says כשר.

steps.title: Why do we need this משנה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this משנה is needed. The first משנה of the מסכת already taught that the agent must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need all this again? It was already taught once: 'One who brings a גט from overseas must say: It was written in front of me and it was signed in front of me!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole משנה. It looks like a repeat of the very first משנה of מסכת גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the agent must say both parts, then it is obvious that seeing only part, or splitting the testimony, is not good enough. So the גמרא asks what new point this משנה adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this again?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why do I need this further teaching?
Didn't it already teach this once:
"One who brings a גט from a land overseas
phrases.notes: This is quoting the very first משנה of מסכת גיטין.

phrases.english: must say: 'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence'"!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה just presented is needed at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first משנה already requires the full statement, so this משנה looks like a repeat.

steps.title: The first משנה could be read as only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: From the first משנה alone, one might think the statement is only the proper way to do it from the start, and the גט is still כשר without it. This משנה teaches that without it the גט is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that משנה, I would have said: he should say it, but if he did not say it, the גט is still valid. So this משנה teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this משנה adds something new. Without the full statement, the גט is actually פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'צריך' (must) in the first משנה could mean 'should, from the start' (לכתחילה). This משנה, by saying 'פסול,' shows that the statement is required even after the fact (בדיעבד).

keyTerms.meaning: The ideal way from the start / after the fact

steps.whatToRemember: The agent's statement is not just the ideal way. Without it, the גט is פסול even after the fact.

phrases.english: If we learned it from that one only, I would have said:
he is required to say it, but if he did not say it, the גט is valid;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the משנה teaches a new point that was not clear before
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement is needed only from the start; without it, the גט is still כשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the statement, the גט is פסול even after the fact.

steps.title: Which half was written in front of him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the case of 'half was written in my presence, and all was signed in my presence' (פסול) and asks which half is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Half of it was written in front of me and all of it was signed in front of me': it is invalid. Which half is this talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks a clarifying question about it. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of פסול depends on which part of the גט the agent saw being written. The גמרא needs to pin this down before the ruling makes sense.

phrases.english: "Half of it was written in my presence
and all of it was signed in my presence": it is invalid.
Which half?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a specific case of the משנה (from step 16) to clarify it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which half of the גט the agent saw being written.

steps.title: It cannot be the first half, because of רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: If the first half was written in front of him, the גט should be כשר. רבי אלעזר said that even one line written לשמה is enough, and nothing more needs checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the first half, there is a problem. רבי אלעזר said: even if only one line was written for her sake, nothing more is needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, 'the first half,' and knocks it down using רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, seeing the start of the גט written לשמה is enough. So an agent who saw the whole first half being written has seen more than enough, and the גט should be כשר, not פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: For her sake, written specifically for this woman

phrases.english: If you say it means the first half,
but didn't רבי אלעזר say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא כָּתַב בּוֹ אֶלָּא שִׁיטָה אַחַת לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: even if he wrote only one line of it for her sake,
he no longer needs anything more!
phrases.notes: He means the agent does not need to have seen the rest being written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִלֵּימָא חֶצְיוֹ רִאשׁוֹן, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to step 20 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר says one line written לשמה is enough, so seeing the first half should make the גט כשר.

steps.title: רב אשי: it means the latter half
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the agent saw only the latter half being written, so he did not see the beginning written לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: it means the latter half.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the answer: the case is when the agent saw only the second half being written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the agent did not see the beginning of the גט being written, he cannot testify that it was written לשמה. That is why the גט is פסול.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
It means the latter half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 after step 21 ruled out 'the first half.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Half' means the latter half, so the beginning was not seen being written.

steps.title: רב חסדא: still invalid even if two confirm the second signature
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the case of 'all was written, half was signed in my presence' (פסול). רב חסדא rules that it is פסול even if two people confirm the second witness's signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All of it was written in front of me and half of it was signed in front of me': it is invalid. רב חסדא said: even if two people testify about the second witness's signature, it is still invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה, and רב חסדא adds a surprising ruling about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Half signed' means the agent saw only one witness sign. You might think that two people confirming the other signature fills the gap, but רב חסדא says the גט is still פסול.

phrases.english: "All of it was written in my presence
and half of it was signed in my presence": it is invalid.
phrases.notes: 'Half signed' means he saw only one of the two witnesses sign.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
And even if two people testify
about the signature of the second witness, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא וַאֲפִילּוּ שְׁנַיִם מְעִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case of the משנה and adds רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גט is פסול even if two people confirm the signature that the agent did not see.

steps.title: What is רב חסדא's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the גט is פסול when every signature is covered either by the agent or by two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב חסדא's ruling. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each signature seems to be backed up: one by the agent and one by two people. So the גמרא wants to know what is still missing.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why combining the agent's testimony with two people's confirmation does not make the גט כשר.

steps.title: All one method or all the other
steps.stepSummary: The גט must be proven completely through regular קיום הגט or completely through the תקנת חכמים, not by mixing the two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either the whole thing goes through the regular confirmation of the document, or the whole thing goes through the enactment of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24 by explaining why רב חסדא invalidates the גט: you cannot mix two different ways of proving it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate ways to back up a גט. One is קיום הגט, where witnesses confirm the signatures. The other is the תקנת חכמים, where the agent declares he saw it signed. רב חסדא holds that each method must cover the whole גט, so half from the agent and half from two people does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Confirming the גט the normal way, by witnesses who confirm the signatures
The rule the Sages set up, here the agent's declaration that he saw the גט written and signed
All of it, the whole thing

phrases.english: Either all of it through confirmation of the document,
or all of it through the enactment of the Sages.
phrases.notes: This is the agent saying 'it was written and signed in front of me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בְּקִיּוּם הַגֵּט, אוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בְּתַקָּנַת חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 by giving רב חסדא's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the גט is פסול when every signature is covered by either the agent or two people.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two methods of proof cannot be combined. The whole גט must rest on one method.

steps.title: Can two people be worse than one?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: if the agent alone had confirmed the second signature, the גט would be כשר. So how can confirmation by two people make it פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenges this: Is there anything where if one person says it, it is valid, but now that there are two, it is invalid?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the 'no mixing' reasoning by pointing out that it leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the agent had said he also saw the second witness sign, one person's word would make the גט כשר. Here two people confirm that same signature, which is stronger testimony. רבא finds it unreasonable that more and stronger testimony would make the גט פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, he challenges it

phrases.english: Rava objects to this:
Is there anything
where, if one said it, it is valid;
phrases.notes: The 'one' is the agent. If he alone said he saw the second signature, the גט would be fine.

phrases.english: now that there are two, it is invalid?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 25 for רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'all one method' reasoning behind רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two people's testimony is stronger than one. If one person's word makes the גט כשר, two people's word should not make it פסול.

steps.title: רבא begins his own explanation
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the earlier reasoning, רבא starts to give his own explanation with the word 'even'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא says: Even...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבא is starting a new explanation, and the rest of his words continue on the next part of the דף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that רבא is dropping the explanation he just challenged. He now begins his own explanation with the word אפילו, and the rest of it continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava says: Even

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his challenge in step 26, רבא opens his own way of explaining the case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא begins a new explanation of the case. The content continues beyond this section.
